strongest_bounded_proposition: Sources confirm servile/slave categories in the wider ancient Caucasus and much earlier temple slaves in Albania, but the bounded packet does not establish a significant slavery institution in Caucasian Albania at c.500 CE.
strongest_unsupported_proposition: Do not infer fifth-century Albanian slavery from ancient Strabo-era temple slaves or from later Caucasian slave-export histories.
territorial_practice_summary: Exact fifth-century territorial practice remains unresolved.
terminology_category_qualification: Servile, dependent, temple-slave and later exported-captive categories span different periods and institutions.
temporal_scope_precision: The strongest direct Albania slavery reference is ancient and not contemporaneous with 500 CE.
inference_extent: No fifth-century prevalence or structural-significance claim.
contrary_limiting_evidence: A classic specialist synthesis explicitly cautions that slavery does not appear to have flourished on an extensive scale in Caucasia.
language_access_limitations: English-accessible research packet only; non-English and non-digitized scholarship was not exhaustively searched.

sources.title: Introduction to Christian Caucasian History: The Formative Centuries (IVth–VIIIth)
sources.author: Cyril Toumanoff

unresolved_issues: No direct c.500 slavery-status evidence established.
